title: MingCute Screenshot Quality Recovery batch 095
review_goal: Differentiate umbrella and vector bezier variants with screenshot grounded depicts and deterministic evidence fields.

items.depicts_observation: Half circle umbrella canopy above one straight shaft ending in one curved hook handle
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a classic rain umbrella with a vertical shaft and hooked handle.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the leaning beach umbrella when the canopy should sit on an angled pole over a base.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot shows the straight shaft and hook handle of a rain umbrella rather than a leaning beach umbrella stand.

items.depicts_observation: Leaning beach umbrella canopy above one angled pole and one low ground base
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants an umbrella fixed to the ground at an angle instead of a handheld rain umbrella.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the hook handled umbrella when the canopy should not sit on a low base with a leaning pole.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot plants the canopy on an angled pole and base instead of hanging it from a hook handle.

items.depicts_observation: Bezier path with one top bar linking two top nodes and two lower branch nodes
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants the bezier cue to branch downward from a top handle bar into two lower nodes.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the S path bezier or the square node frame when the icon should not reduce to one loose curve or one closed box.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot is the only bezier variant with a top handle bar and two lower branching node paths.

items.depicts_observation: Curved bezier path linking four square nodes across one loose S shaped line
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants the bezier cue to read as one flowing curve through several nodes.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the branched top bar bezier or the closed square node frame when the path should stay one loose curve.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot uses one flowing S style curve through four nodes instead of a branch or a closed square frame.

items.depicts_observation: Square outline built from four corner nodes connected by four straight segments
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants the bezier cue to read as a closed square frame anchored by four corner nodes.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the branched bezier or the S curve bezier when the icon should not open into branches or flowing curves.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot closes the nodes into a square frame instead of branching them or linking them with one loose curve.
